docs.title: Hello, There!
docs.text:
Welcome to the BoronEngine documentation.

This is the official documentation for BoronEngine.

docs.title: Downloading BoronEngine from GitHub Releases
docs.text: First go to the github releases, then download the latest version of BoronEngine and un-zip the folder and doubleclick the .exe and wait 30~ secunds to the BoronEngine folder to be copied to %AppData% and then you are good!

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
To run BoronEngine, you have two options:

  1. Download the latest release

Download the pre-built BoronEngine executable from GitHub Releases.

Learn how to download and run BoronEngine

  1. Build BoronEngine from source

Download the source code, configure the project with CMake, build it, and then run BoronEngine.

Follow these steps:

  1. Check the build requirements
  2. Download and build the source code

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A code editor or IDE

  • CMake 3.10 or newer

  • A C++23-compatible compiler

  • Supported Vulkan API versions:

    • Vulkan 1.0
    • Vulkan 1.1
    • Vulkan 1.2
    • Vulkan 1.3
    • Vulkan 1.4

  • Windows

    Linux support is planned for a future version of BoronEngine.

docs.title: Downloading the BoronEngine Source Code
docs.text:
First, go to the BoronEngine GitHub page.

Click the Code button and either download the source code as a .zip file or clone the repository using Git.

Once you have downloaded the source code, open the project folder in your code editor's terminal or in Command Prompt.

Configure the project using CMake:

cmake -S . -B build

Then choose whether you want to build BoronEngine in Release or Debug mode.

Release:

cmake --build build --config Release

Debug:

cmake --build build --config Debug

The compiled files will be located in the build directory.
